event.title: College of Business Master in Cybersecurity Fly-In
event.address: 601 New Jersey Ave NW Suite 103 Washington, D.C. 20001
event.description:
The College of Business Master in Cybersecurity DC Fly-In is a two-day experiential seminar designed to give students a firsthand look at the intersection of cybersecurity, technology, policy, and national security in Washington, D.C. Students will engage with experts across government, industry, academia, and the broader cybersecurity community to explore how policy is developed and how cybersecurity professionals are shaping the future.

The Fly-In will provide opportunities to learn about cybersecurity careers in the nation’s capital, engage in conversations with leaders working across the field, and gain a deeper understanding of the policies and challenges influencing the cybersecurity landscape. Students will also have the opportunity to explore policy solutions and participate in advocacy meetings on Capitol Hill, connecting their academic experience to real-world issues and opportunities in Washington, D.C.

event.title: Seminar (SIPA1-100): Tomoki Fujii
event.location_name: SIPA - School of International & Public Affairs
event.address: 11200 SW 8th ST, School of Intl & Pub Affairs, Miami, Florida 33199
event.description:
"Agricultural Seasonality and Conditional Cash Transfer: Evidence from a Randomized Field Experiment in Bangladesh", by Tomoki Fujii, Singapore Management University (Venue: SIPA1-100)

Tomoki Fujii is Deputy Dean and Professor of Economics at the School of Economics, Singapore Management University.  His research covers broadly applied areas of microeconomics, including development, education, environment, and health. He received a PhD in Multidisciplinary Science from the University of Tokyo and PhD in Agricultural and Resource Economics from the University of California, Berkeley. His website is here.

event.title: iWitness Lunch Break at MMC: The Creation and Activation of Archives
event.description:
This Lunch Break is part of the National Museum of American History’s (NMAH) National Youth Summit, which brings middle and high school students together with scholars, teachers, policy experts and activists for a national conversation about important events in America’s past and their relevance to the nation’s present and future.

As a starting point for this conversation, our team—Dr. Gabriela Portela (School of Communication), Marianne Lamonaca (The Humanities Edge) and Dr. Aarti Mehta-Kroll (Public Humanities Lab)—worked with NMAH staff to select a hat worn by Savas Zahvala Castro while he was a manual laborer, or bracero, in California.

The Emergency Farm Labor Program, commonly known as the Bracero Program (1942–1964), recruited approximately two million Mexican nationals to come to the United States on short-term labor contracts. Photographs taken by Leonard Nadel in the late 1950s and early 1960s, together with oral histories and artifacts collected as part of the Bracero History Project, form an archive that allows us to continue exploring the program’s impact on American society.

Our invited panelists—Christine Malcolm (Profiles in Black Miami), Dr. Marta Giercyzk (Department of English) and Jeff Guin (Vizcaya Museum and Gardens)—will discuss how they have engaged in community-based historical research using textual, oral history and artifact-based methodologies. They will invite the audience to consider how we can preserve community stories today, capturing the specificity and nuance that may offer future generations valuable insights into this moment in history.

 

11:30 AM – 12:00 PM: Lunch

12:00 PM – 12:30 PM: Panel discussion

12:30 PM – 1:00 PM: Q&A

 

This event is presented in partnership with iWitness, a dynamic, multifaceted community nonprofit that works closely with the Green School’s Public Humanities Lab. Through initiatives such as the Global Borderless Caribbean Initiative, iWitness invites us to engage in visual storytelling, critical reflection and civic dialogue, focusing on issues that impact and shape communities in Latin America and the Caribbean and their global diasporas.

event.title: Qudit-Based Quantum Computing with Rick Mukherjee, Ph.D.
event.address: 10555 W Flagler ST, Engineering Center, Miami, Florida 33174
event.description:
Join us for the first talk in the FIU Quantum Distinguished Speaker Series. The series brings researchers from across the field to FIU to share new ideas in quantum science.

Rick Mukherjee, Ph.D., opens the series. He is an associate professor of physics at the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga and inaugural director of its UTC Quantum Center.

Mukherjee will start with an overview of the UTC Quantum Center’s research. Then he will explain how qudits, which have more than two levels, whereas qubits have two, could help solve hard optimization problems more efficiently than qubit-based methods.

Attend in person at the Engineering Center or join live on Zoom from anywhere.
